expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof glues smooth algebraic-space presentations across a thickening and transfers their compatible maps into a representing space by the pushout universal property. Essential surjectivity is constructed on a new smooth cover and combined with the fully faithful descent calculation.

expected.title: Internal Hom on an affine scheme computes the algebraic Hom for a coherent first argument
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian ring A with X = Spec(A) and K, L in D(A) with K in D_Coh(A) and L of finite injective dimension, the lemma asserts RSheafHom_{O_X}(K~, L~) = the tilde of RHom_A(K, L) in D(O_X) (statement lines 365-376). The proof assumes L is given by a finite complex I^bullet of injective A-modules, and by induction on the length and compatibility with distinguished triangles reduces to L = I[0] with I injective (proof lines 378-385). In that case Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom identifies the n-th cohomology sheaf of RSheafHom_{O_X}(K~, L~) as the sheaf associated to the presheaf D(f) -> Ext^n_{A_f}(K otimes_A A_f, I otimes_A A_f) (proof lines 386-395). Since A is Noetherian the localisation I otimes_A A_f is injective by Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-localization-injective-modules, so the Ext computes as Hom_{A_f}(H^{-n}(K otimes_A A_f), I otimes_A A_f) = Hom_{A_f}(H^{-n}(K) otimes_A A_f, I otimes_A A_f) = Hom_A(H^{-n}(K), I) otimes_A A_f, the last step because H^{-n}(K) is a finite A-module by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-hom-from-finitely-presented (proof lines 396-410). This identifies both sides and the proof is done (proof lines 410-412). Reducing along triangles to a single injective and then computing the presheaf of Exts on a basis of principal opens is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

expected.title: Pushforward of a principal divisor along a dominant proper morphism equals the divisor of the norm
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the pushforward of the divisor of a rational function along a dominant proper morphism between integral schemes of the same dimension as the divisor of the norm of that function (statement lines 2644-2656, tag 02RT). The proof reduces to comparing coefficients at an integral closed subscheme of codimension one, uses the codimension one finiteness statement to make the morphism finite over an affine neighbourhood, rewrites both coefficients in ring theoretic terms as an order and as a sum of residue degrees times orders, and concludes with the norm compatibility statement for finite extensions of dimension one. The reduction to the finite case is the substance, so the claim is H2.

expected.title: K-injective limits of truncation resolutions and derived completeness
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof builds the ordinary inverse limit of split-surjective injective resolutions degree by degree. It constructs a termwise split product exact sequence proving that this limit is both K-injective and the derived truncation limit, then identifies the canonical comparison from the original complex. The criterion exposes precisely the obstruction to using truncation resolutions in the unbounded category.
